Song Coach

This page is opened from a local file, so Chrome won't allow Bluetooth, MIDI or the microphone. Open it from its https:// web address instead.

Add a song

Pick an audio file (MP3, WAV, M4A) and the app turns it into notes on your phone. You can also add MIDI or MusicXML files, several at once with Add several MIDI files. Got a song file from someone with Song Coach? Tap Add a shared song file: it's ready to play straight away, no scanning or API key needed. For Suno songs, download the piano or melody stem; full-band mixes convert poorly.

Write your own music

Play on your piano or on the keys on screen, and Song Coach writes the sheet music as you go. Save it and it joins your library as an original, signed with your name.

No recordings yet. Open a song, tap Rec at the bottom, play, then tap Stop. Your takes show up here.

Make a playlist to play several songs one after another.

🎤 Karaoke Pick a song and sing along. The words light up as you go, and the microphone scores how well you hit each note.

No songs of your own yet. Open Add a song to bring one in, or try one from Samples.

Read sheet music

Create one at console.anthropic.com → API keys, then paste it here. It's saved only on this phone and sent only to Anthropic. Each page usually costs a few cents.

Account and sync

Sign in on each of your phones and tablets, and your songs, scores, stars, streaks, playlists and favorites stay the same on all of them. Everything still works offline; changes sync when you're back online. Your API key, piano connection and sound settings stay on each device.
Sync needs a Firebase project first. Paste its web app config here (Firebase console → Project settings → Your apps).

☁️

Backup and other devices

A backup is one file with all your songs and playlists (not your API key). Keep it on your phone or in Google Drive, then open the app on your other device and tap Restore.
Fix storage
  1. Tap Save backup to my phone above first, so nothing is lost.
  2. In Chrome, tap the icon left of the web address → Permissions (or Site settings). Make sure On-device site data (or Cookies and site data) is Allowed.
  3. If it already is, tap Delete data / Clear & reset for this site there. That repairs Chrome's damaged storage for the app.
  4. Reopen the app, then Restore from a backup and pick the file you saved.

Covers and lyrics

Owner tools

Only you see this section, when you're signed in as yourself.

When you press Play in Wait or Play mode
Showcase: the song plays itself in perfect time, and the screen shows every key hit perfectly, with full points, combos, stars and leaderboard credit. Your own keys are ignored. Great for videos.
Magic: with a piano connected, any key you press plays the right notes in the song.
App usage How many devices use Song Coach, which phones, tablets, systems and browsers, which app version each one has, any errors they hit, and who's signed in.

How it works

Privacy: to make sure the app works everywhere, it counts which kinds of devices use it (model, system, browser, screen size, app version and any errors) with a random ID made on this device. If you sign in, your name and email are included. Nothing else is collected, and recordings, songs and your voice never leave your device.
Karaoke (on the songs page) plays a song with its words for you to sing. The microphone listens and scores how much of each note you sing on pitch, in any octave. Turn off Guide melody to sing without the tune playing.
Wait stops the notes until you press the right keys on the piano.
Play keeps time and scores each note you hit within a quarter second.
Listen plays the song on your piano so you can hear it first.
Aa switches a song with words between falling notes and big words with the chords above them. The keyboard still lights the keys to play.
Key − and + move the whole song down or up a half step, for an easier key or a singer's range.
Songs with chord symbols get a Guitar button: chords scroll down with finger positions on the neck, and Listen strums them.
Turn your phone sideways for the widest keyboard.

Connect your piano

Looking for your piano…

Use one option. Bluetooth MIDI is the most accurate: the piano tells the app exactly which keys you press, including chords.

Bluetooth MIDI (recommended) On your piano, make sure Bluetooth MIDI is on. Close any other piano app first (like Kawai PianoRemote), since only one app can connect at a time.
Don't pair the piano in your phone's Bluetooth settings for this. That pairing is for music audio. The app connects to the piano's MIDI itself when you tap Find my piano.
USB cable or already-paired MIDI For a USB-C to USB-B cable into the piano's USB to Host port.
Phone microphone Backup option. Hears one note at a time and can mistake octaves, so it is forgiving about octave.

Read sheet music

Add the pages in any order; they're sorted by their page numbers. Claude reads the notes, the words and the tempo marking on each page. A busy page can take a minute or two. Keep pages flat, well lit and fully in frame.

Reading sheet music needs an Anthropic API key.

Magic mode with your piano

Tap any key in the song's rhythm and the piano plays the right notes. Press harder to play louder.

The app just asked the piano to stop sounding the keys you press (this is called Local Control), so you only hear the song's notes. It turns it back on when you leave Magic.

If you still hear the key you pressed along with the right notes, your piano didn't accept the request. Turn Local Control off in the piano's MIDI settings, or in Kawai's PianoRemote app, and turn it back on when you're done. Turning the piano off and on also turns it back on.
